title: Is This Data Identifying?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Classify eight data fields as a direct identifier, identifying in combination, or not identifying.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify eight data fields as direct identifiers, identifiers in combination, or not identifying, correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Student data, personally identifiable data, direct identifier, indirect identifier, and small-group identification, from the section "What Counts as Student Data" in Chapter 10

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, get feedback with the reason, and review what was missed
keyQuestions: Does this field point to one student on its own?
Could it point to one student when combined with other facts?
commonMisconceptions: Group data can never identify a person
Only a name or ID number counts as identifying
assessmentOpportunities: A report shows the average reading score for one class of 28 students. Which category?
A spreadsheet has no names but lists birth date, ZIP code, and gender. Is it anonymous?
Can group data ever identify a person?

controls.name: Choice buttons
controls.description: commit an answer. A wrong first answer gives a hint and lets you choose again; only the first answer counts.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: opens or closes the reference table. Reading it is exploration, not evidence.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next item after feedback. On the results screen, Previous missed and Next missed step through what you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: starts a practice run with the items reshuffled. Practice runs do not change the first-run score.
